hero.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader as caucus debates strategy
hero.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode about a potential bid. Van Hollen said the party should not have a coronation and that he has not shut the door on a challenge to Schumer, who is currently minority leader and widely expected to be elected to lead the new Senate majority in January.

Van Hollen's comments come as some Senate Democrats have withheld support for Schumer while seeking clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years. Democrats are scheduled to meet as a group Tuesday to discuss their path forward. Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who met with Van Hollen on Monday, said she will not vote for a majority leader candidate who cannot articulate a plan, especially for the first 100 days. Slotkin declined over the weekend to rule out her own leadership ambitions.

Both Van Hollen and Slotkin are viewed as potential presidential contenders. Van Hollen had previously suggested his focus was on 2028 and ensuring Democrats win back the White House.

Schumer needs only a majority of the Democratic caucus to win the leadership election during a closed-door meeting scheduled for early December. Many Senate Democrats have expressed support for Schumer following the party's performance in last week's midterm elections. Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut said Monday he plans to continue supporting Schumer but added that the Senate needs new ideas, energy from incoming members, and changes in how it operates.

The tower, located in the Saudi capital's financial district, was hit by a missile or drone strike that shattered windows across multiple floors. No casualties were reported.

cards.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
cards.teaser: House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure.

cards.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C

Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation. Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

hero.headline: Krakow mass shooting suspect dies in hospital as Polish prosecutors say motive investigation continues
hero.teaser: The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol
hero.body:
The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Polish man was shot by police officers within three minutes of opening fire in the city's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. He had been hospitalized with injuries sustained during a gunfight with responding officers.

Polish prosecutors said Monday that investigations into the suspect's motive remain ongoing, walking back earlier statements by a government minister who described the gunman as inspired by far-right ideologies and ultra-nationalism. Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, told reporters the motive inquiry continues. The suspect has not been officially named.

The attack killed four Polish citizens, a British national, and an Austrian woman in the Main Market Square. Police later found three bodies at the gunman's home, identified as his 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister. Authorities seized four firearms from the suspect's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition. Polish media reported the suspect held a firearms permit.

Sixteen people were hospitalized after the shooting, including two police officers who were injured during the gunfight with the suspect. A surgeon who was eating nearby when the attack began rushed to the scene and helped treat victims before ambulances arrived. Professor Michał Pędziwiatr said his colleague used his hand to stem bleeding from a severely injured police officer, and that intervention undoubtedly saved the officer's life. Both wounded officers have since emerged from comas.

Poland declared two days of national mourning following the attack. Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited Krakow and said the country had not previously experienced such drastic terrorism.

cards.headline: Explosion at Turkish steel factory kills at least 17 workers
cards.teaser: A crane collapse during maintenance at a major facility near Izmir caused the blast. Authorities have arrested five people.
cards.body:
At least 17 workers died and 12 others were injured in an explosion at the Habas Demir Celik iron and steel factory near Izmir in western Turkey. The blast occurred around midday when a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed during scheduled maintenance on an electric arc furnace, causing materials to fall into the furnace below. Footage showed a large fire and towering column of smoke at the facility in Aliaga, one of the country's leading steel producers.

Authorities arrested at least five people as investigations continued. Some people were believed to remain under rubble. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan confirmed the deaths and said search and rescue operations were ongoing. Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, according to an independent labor watchdog.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.

Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.headline: Krakow gunman killed his parents and sister before Main Market Square attack that left six dead
cards.teaser: The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.
cards.body:
The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.

The 25-year-old Polish man drove into the square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car, killing four women and two men including a British national before armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes. A minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by far-right ideologies and described him as an ultra-nationalist.

hero.headline: ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at routine check-in after TPS termination, prompting San Diego school district response
hero.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him to federal custody, according to school officials and an advocacy group. The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School, lost his Temporary Protected Status protections this summer after a Supreme Court decision allowed President Donald Trump to end TPS for Haitians. He was summoned to meet with ICE officers Wednesday, and his uncle brought him to the appointment to comply with the law, according to a letter San Diego Unified School District officials sent Friday to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Health and Human Services.

ICE officers determined the boy to be an unaccompanied minor after the uncle could not establish legal guardianship, according to a DHS spokesperson. The agency said it removed the boy from the household out of caution to ensure his safety. The boy was subsequently transferred to the Office of Refugee Resettlement, which takes custody of children deemed unaccompanied minors. As of Monday, his family did not know where he was being held, according to Representative Juan Vargas.

The boy had been living with his uncle and cousins after his father was deported last year, according to the school district and the Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigrant rights advocacy group. TPS is a humanitarian designation that had shielded hundreds of thousands of Haitians from deportation following the country's 2010 earthquake. The protections were renewed multiple times as Haiti descended into crisis, with gangs now controlling much of the capital after the president was assassinated in 2021.

The school district said it is sending crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School this week because the boy's classmates have expressed concern and fear for him. School officials asked DHS and HHS to reconsider how immigration enforcement policies are affecting students, but as of Monday had received no response. The Office of Refugee Resettlement said it does not comment on specific cases. The boy is among 1,640 children considered unaccompanied minors currently in HHS care.

A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air

Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney. Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher.

cards.headline: Six killed in shooting in Krakow, Poland; British citizen among dead
cards.teaser: A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo
cards.body:
A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo

A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

cards.headline: Arrest made in shooting that killed one during Winston-Salem State University homecoming weekend
cards.teaser: Authorities arrested a 20-year-old man in connection with a shooting that killed one person and injured another during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North
cards.body:
Authorities arrested a 20-year-old man in connection with a shooting that killed one person and injured another during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North

Ziyaire Antonyo Spinks faces charges of murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill inflicting serious injury, and felony possession of a firearm on an educational campus, Winston-Salem Police Department said Sunday. The shooting Saturday night killed Peyton Izaia Patterson, 19, and injured Alyssa Janae Ellerbee, 19, who was treated at a hospital and released.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

hero.headline: Qantas to outsource 850 jobs to Accenture, most moving to India
hero.body:
Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial intelligence and information technology modernization. Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson announced the plan in an internal email to staff on Tuesday, saying the job cuts will begin in mid-2027.

The outsourcing will start with finance, procurement, human resources, and marketing roles shifting mostly to teams in India and some to Australia. Hudson said the airline is seeking to modernize its IT systems and cited the rapid pace of technological change. Qantas spends more than 1 billion Australian dollars annually on technology and operates more than 1,000 legacy applications that were not designed to work together, she said.

Under the multi-year deal with Accenture, Qantas aims to redesign and simplify corporate functions and reduce duplication so staff can focus on work that creates value for customers and the business, Hudson said. The company said the work transferred to Accenture will eventually be transformed further with automation and artificial intelligence.

Qantas employs approximately 28,000 staff in Australia and 4,000 globally. The announcement comes days after the airline issued a market update indicating fare increases and flight reductions due to higher fuel costs. Hudson acknowledged the difficulty of the news, telling staff she was sorry for the uncertainty it brings. The airline said it is in talks with unions and staff on the plans.

cards.headline: Skydance outlines $6 billion in cost savings, HBO Max-Paramount+ bundle in first earnings report after Warner Bros. Discovery deal
cards.teaser: The company plans to save on overhead, marketing, technology, and procurement while launching a streaming bundle in early 2027.
cards.body:
Skydance outlined plans for at least $6 billion in cost savings in its first earnings report after completing its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The company expects $2.2 billion in savings from corporate overhead and real estate, $1 billion from marketing, $1.2 billion from technology consolidation, and $1.4 billion from procurement and vendor management, according to CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz.

Skydance announced plans to launch a bundle combining HBO Max and Paramount+ in early 2027, with the services remaining distinct similar to Disney's approach with Hulu. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $7 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1 billion, though results do not include Warner Bros. Discovery because the deal closed after the quarter ended.

cards.headline: Lucid misses earnings estimates, secures $1.75 billion loan expansion from Saudi fund
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker reported a wider-than-expected loss while extending its cash runway into 2027.
cards.body:
Lucid Group on Monday reported third-quarter revenue of $350 million and a loss of $2.74 per share, missing Wall Street estimates of $407 million in revenue and a loss of $2.28 per share. The electric vehicle maker also announced a $1.75 billion increase in a delayed draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, its largest shareholder.

The additional capital is expected to fund operations and key investments into the fourth quarter of 2027, including the start of production for a planned midsize vehicle. The loan expansion brings Lucid's total liquidity to $3.75 billion, up from $2 billion at the end of the third quarter.

cards.headline: Hims & Hers reports 49% revenue growth but swings to net loss as margins compress
cards.teaser: The telehealth company's third-quarter revenue reached $890 million, up from $599 million a year earlier, but gross margin fell to 57% from 74%.
cards.body:
Hims & Hers Health reported third-quarter revenue of $890.4 million, a 49% increase from $599 million in the same period last year, but swung to a net loss of $33 million compared to net income of $15.8 million a year earlier. The telehealth company's gross margin fell to 57% from 74% in the third quarter of 2025.

The company projected fourth-quarter revenue of $875 million to $895 million with adjusted EBITDA of $70 million to $90 million, reflecting a margin of 8% to 10%. Chief Financial Officer Yemi Okupe said the company intentionally paced marketing spending ahead of planned platform expansions in the fourth quarter.

cards.headline: Rocket Lab reports record revenue and $515 million in Neutron contracts as debut slips to 2027
cards.teaser: The space company posted revenue gains and backlog growth in its third quarter but pushed its Neutron rocket's first launch back a year.
cards.body:
Rocket Lab reported record third-quarter revenue and a 52 percent sequential increase in backlog, reaching $1.2 billion, the company announced Monday. The space launch provider signed $515 million in new contracts for its Neutron rocket and posted positive operating cash flow.

The company's stock fell despite the revenue beat, as Rocket Lab pushed the debut of its Neutron vehicle to 2027. The company missed earnings-per-share expectations for the quarter and guided to record revenue and gross margin expansion in the fourth quarter.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO hired crisis PR firm a year before acknowledging affair linked to espionage investigation
cards.teaser: Jensen Huang retained Heller Inc., which specializes in scandal management, at least a year before disclosing a relationship with a woman suspected of Chinese intelligence ties.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hired crisis communications firm Heller Inc. at least a year before publicly acknowledging an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, Wired reported. The firm, led by Risa Heller and known for advising clients through sex scandals, was copied on press inquiries about Huang shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report examined whether Nvidia was helping Chinese companies evade U.S. export controls.

On Sunday, Huang acknowledged an affair with a former Megaspeed executive without naming her. Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation, citing reports that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." Neither Nvidia nor Heller responded to requests for comment.

Nvidia stock fell sharply Monday after the board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe was a Chinese intelligence operative.

Nvidia shares fell approximately 4 percent by close of trading Monday, erasing about $250 billion in market value, following the company's announcement that its board would conduct an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The board action came after Huang admitted in a company message that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed, whom U.S.

hero.headline: Wyndham exposed millions of customer records after hardcoded password found in Android app
hero.body:
Hotel giant Wyndham acknowledged a security incident after a researcher discovered a hardcoded password in its Android app that granted access to an internal database containing personal information for millions of rewards members. Security researcher Robert Wiggins found the credential embedded in the app's source code, which allowed access to a Salesforce-hosted database storing customer names, email addresses, member numbers, and login tokens.

The database contained millions of entries from Wyndham's 129 million enrolled rewards members, though Wiggins could not determine an exact count of exposed records. The credential was revoked after Wiggins contacted Wyndham through a journalist because the company had no public channel for reporting security vulnerabilities. A Wyndham spokesperson said the company addressed the issue and found no evidence of unauthorized access, but declined to say whether server logs existed to verify that claim.

Wyndham would not disclose how long the password was embedded in the app, whether it plans to notify affected customers, or whether it will report the incident to the Securities and Exchange Commission as required for material cybersecurity events at public companies. Hardcoded credentials are considered a critical security weakness because anyone with the software can extract and use the password, and such vulnerabilities typically receive maximum severity ratings.

This marks the second major discovery of hardcoded credentials by Wiggins in two weeks, following a similar flaw in the Applebee's app. Wiggins used artificial intelligence tools to scan decompiled app code for such weaknesses. Wyndham's cybersecurity director provided an email address for researchers to report issues, but the company declined to say whether it would establish a formal vulnerability disclosure program or update its website to publicize the reporting channel.

Wyndham experienced a separate security incident in 2024 when hotel check-in computers were found running remote-access spyware that leaked guest records to the internet. That spyware company was later hacked and shut down, and its owner was convicted of making and selling unlawful spyware.

cards.headline: Anthropic to set IPO valuation range this week despite Nasdaq sell-off
cards.teaser: The AI company plans to begin trading next week as investors seek a gauge of the industry's strength.
cards.body:
Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, according to The Wall Street Journal. The AI company is moving forward with its listing despite a recent major Nasdaq sell-off.

Some institutional investors are now pushing for a valuation below the $1.5 trillion target discussed as recently as last week, which was itself considerably below the $2 trillion floated a few months ago, the Journal reported. Rival OpenAI was reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion last week after raising $11 billion in fresh capital, short of the $20 billion it had initially sought.

cards.headline: Trump says he was briefed on Nvidia CEO's alleged spy relationship but claims it 'didn't make much of an impact'
cards.teaser: President acknowledged intelligence memo may have mentioned Jensen Huang's ties to suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, though he remained vague on timing.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump acknowledged at a White House press briefing that he may have been briefed on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, though he said it "didn't make much of an impact" on him. The New York Times previously reported Trump was briefed roughly a year ago and that Secretary of State Marco Rubio helped draft a memo on the relationship before Trump's May visit to China.

Trump said Huang told him he had "no idea" the person was a spy. The president declined to specify when he first learned of the relationship and said he would not raise the matter with Chinese President Xi Jinping next week, adding he believes Huang is "a very honorable man."

cards.headline: Short seller flagged Nvidia CEO's ties to suspected spy months before scandal
cards.teaser: Culper Research highlighted Jensen Huang's relationship with a Megaspeed executive in a May report, before espionage allegations emerged.
cards.body:
Short seller Culper Research questioned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive now suspected of being a Chinese spy, in a May report six months before the scandal became public. The firm described their connection as uncomfortably close, noting multiple social appearances together and suggesting some Nvidia employees wondered about a special relationship between the two.

Huang admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and Nvidia has opened a formal investigation. Intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on the CEO and influence his position on U.S. export controls for advanced AI chips. Culper's report also alleged Megaspeed was secretly financed by Alibaba, a claim the Financial Times partially confirmed Monday.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO hired crisis PR firm a year before acknowledging affair
cards.teaser: Jensen Huang engaged Heller Inc., known for handling sex scandals, at least a year before publicly confirming a relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hired crisis communications firm Heller Inc. at least a year before he publicly acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, Wired reported. Heller Inc. founder Risa Heller has advised prominent men through personal scandals and sexual misconduct accusations, including former congressman Anthony Weiner and celebrity chef Mario Batali.

Nvidia's internal communications team was told to copy Heller Inc. on press inquiries about Huang shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report examined whether Nvidia was helping Chinese companies evade U.S. export controls. On Sunday, Huang acknowledged an affair with a former Megaspeed executive, and Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation citing reports that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

cards.headline: Geothermal company Fervo reports $11.9 billion in contracted revenue as it races to power AI data centers
cards.teaser: The company is building a 396-megawatt plant for Google in Utah by 2028 as tech firms seek electricity for data centers.
cards.body:
Geothermal company Fervo reported Monday that it now has $11.9 billion in contracted revenue, up from $7.2 billion last quarter. The company is building a 396-megawatt power plant for Google in Utah, set to connect to the grid by the end of 2028, as technology companies search for electricity to power artificial intelligence data centers.

Fervo connected its first 100-megawatt power plant to the grid earlier this year at Cape Station in Utah. The company reported an operating loss of $43.7 million for the quarter but holds $1.9 billion in cash. Construction costs have dropped from $7,000 per kilowatt for its initial project to $5,500 per kilowatt for the Google plant.

cards.headline: Apple patches security flaws in Messages and AirPlay with iOS 27.2.1
cards.teaser: The update fixes vulnerabilities that could have allowed uninvited access to group chats and attempts to bypass pairing protections.
cards.body:
Apple released iOS 27.2.1 on Monday with security fixes addressing vulnerabilities in Messages, AirPlay, and Bluetooth. The update patches a flaw that could have allowed a remote attacker to join an iMessage group chat without an invitation, along with an issue that might have let an attacker within Bluetooth range bypass rate limits on AirPlay pairing code attempts.

Apple also released corresponding security updates for macOS, watchOS, and visionOS. Many of the fixes apply across platforms due to shared code, and Apple credited researchers who identified the vulnerabilities.

hero.headline: Reds first baseman Sal Stewart wins NL Rookie of the Year after 32-homer, 112-RBI season
hero.body:
Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart won the National League Rookie of the Year award, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday. Stewart received 20 of 30 first-place votes and was the only player in the NL field to appear in the top five on every ballot. The award also earns Cincinnati a bonus pick after the first round of the 2027 draft through the Prospect Promotion Incentive.

Stewart led NL rookies with 700 plate appearances and hit .263/.330/.457 with 32 home runs and 112 RBI. His home run total was 12 more than any other rookie in the league, while his RBI count was nearly 40 ahead of any other first-year player. He finished eighth in the NL in home runs and trailed only Cardinals first baseman Alec Burleson in RBI among all league hitters. Stewart started 110 games at first base, 33 at third base, 11 as a designated hitter, and seven at second base.

Mets outfielder Carson Benge finished second with seven first-place votes and Cardinals middle infielder JJ Wetherholt placed third with three first-place votes. Benge hit .282/.346/.430 with a 20-20 season and was one of the best hitters in the NL after the All-Star Break. Wetherholt appeared to be Stewart's top competition for much of the season but struggled in the second half around a two-week absence due to right wrist tendinitis. Both Benge and Wetherholt were Gold Glove finalists at their positions.

Park adjustments for Cincinnati's hitter-friendly stadium and Stewart's lack of defensive value limited his standing in advanced metrics. Both FanGraphs and Baseball Reference graded Stewart at two wins above replacement, about half the totals for Benge and Wetherholt. The majority of voters prioritized Stewart's power production. All three finalists met Prospect Promotion Incentive criteria and opened the year on their teams' MLB rosters, meaning the winner would secure a bonus pick. Stewart is the Reds' second Rookie of the Year winner this decade and ninth in franchise history.

cards.headline: Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle wins AL Rookie of the Year
cards.teaser: McGonigle received 28 of 30 first-place votes, becoming the sixth Detroit player to win the award.
cards.body:
Detroit Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle won the 2026 American League Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year Award, receiving 28 of 30 first-place votes. McGonigle split time almost equally between shortstop and third base during the season, also appearing as designated hitter in five games.

McGonigle is the sixth Tigers player to win the honor, following Harvey Kuenn in 1953, Mark Fidrych in 1976, Lou Whitaker in 1978, Justin Verlander in 2006, and Michael Fullmer in 2016. Cleveland pitcher Parker Messick finished second in the voting, while Boston's Payton Tolle placed third.

cards.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay questions play call that injured Puka Nacua
cards.teaser: The wide receiver is headed to injured reserve with knee and toe injuries sustained on a handoff late in Sunday's win.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is going on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders. The injuries occurred on the Rams' final offensive play when Nacua took a handoff and rushed for five yards on third-and-11 before being tackled.

Head coach Sean McVay said at a Monday press conference that he has questioned the decision to call that play. McVay said he is kicking himself over the call and feels tremendous responsibility for the injury. With Nacua and Davante Adams now sidelined indefinitely, the Rams may seek receiving help before Tuesday's trade deadline.

cards.headline: College Football Playoff to expand to 24 teams next season
cards.teaser: ESPN and the CFP finalized an agreement to grow the postseason field, a move that will end conference championship games.
cards.body:
ESPN and the College Football Playoff announced Monday they reached an agreement to expand the playoff to 24 teams starting next season. The move will eliminate conference championship games, including the Big 12 title game.

Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark said the conference supported the expansion, stating the 24-team format would deliver more opportunities for programs to compete for a national championship. The expanded playoff drew mixed reactions, though several coaches have expressed support for aligning college football's postseason structure more closely with other sports.

cards.headline: Bills face Vikings on Monday Night Football with Josh Allen leading MVP race
cards.teaser: Buffalo visits Minnesota with quarterback Josh Allen as the MVP favorite, while the Vikings start Carson Wentz with Kyler Murray injured.
cards.body:
The Buffalo Bills face the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football with quarterback Josh Allen entering as the MVP favorite. The Vikings will start Carson Wentz at quarterback with Kyler Murray sidelined by injury.

The matchup is part of Week 9 of the season. Allen has emerged as a leading candidate for league MVP honors heading into the primetime game.

cards.headline: Man Utd expected to sack head coach Michael Carrick
cards.teaser: Board likely to recommend dismissal after worst Premier League start in 40 years
cards.body:
Board likely to recommend dismissal after worst Premier League start in 40 years

Manchester United are increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick following the team's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, which left the club 18th in the Premier League table. Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to recommend Carrick's dismissal to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.

cards.headline: Tom Brady ends ownership stake with Birmingham City
cards.teaser: The NFL legend exits his minority ownership role after three years with the English soccer club.
cards.body:
Tom Brady has ended his association with Birmingham City, the English soccer club announced. The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner in August 2023 when he entered a partnership with the club's owners, Knighthead Capital Management, and served as chairman of an advisory board.

Birmingham thanked Brady for his involvement and support over the past three years. Brady, who retired from the NFL in February 2023, also owns stakes in the Las Vegas Raiders and the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces while working as a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports. Birmingham currently sits atop the Championship standings.

hero.headline: Donnie Dunagan, voice of Bambi in 1942 Disney classic, dies at 92
hero.body:
Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.

Dunagan's brief acting career spanned just seven films over a few years but included two enduring roles. At age four, he made his film debut in 1938's Mother Carey's Chickens. In 1939, he starred in Son of Frankenstein alongside Boris Karloff and Bela Lugosi, playing the son of Baron Wolf von Frankenstein. Walt Disney personally selected Dunagan to be the facial model for Bambi because of his brown eyes, having animators sketch his expressions before offering him the voice role. Dunagan later called the work the thrill of his young life.

After his acting career ended, Dunagan volunteered for the Marines in the early 1950s and served 21 years, including combat in the Korean and Vietnam wars. He earned a Bronze Star and Purple Heart and rose to the rank of major. He kept his Bambi role secret throughout his military service, fearing it would undermine his authority. He said in 2005 that if the troops he led had found out about Bambi, they would have ridden him out on a rail.

Disney tracked Dunagan down in the early 2000s for a DVD release of Bambi, returning him to public life. He became a Disney ambassador and appeared at fan conventions. His agents said Dunagan loved his fans, rallied other veterans, and had an infectious smile and warmth that never lost the childlike spirit of his acting youth.

cards.headline: Jemima Goldsmith accuses ex-boyfriend Russell Brand of violence and coercive control
cards.teaser: The TV producer says she called police to remove Brand from her home during a violent incident in 2014, hours after his sentencing for rape and sexual assault.
cards.body:
Jemima Goldsmith accused ex-boyfriend Russell Brand of violence, coercive control, and abuse during their relationship around 2014. The TV producer said she called police to remove Brand from her home during a violent incident in 2014 but chose not to press charges, citing concerns about press attention affecting her teenage children. Goldsmith made the allegations in a social media statement Monday evening.

Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison Monday after being convicted of raping a woman in 2009 and three counts of sexual assault against three other women. Goldsmith, former wife of ex-Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, said she was glad Brand had faced justice and praised the women who testified at his trial.

cards.headline: Erika Kirk condemns comedians for joking about Charlie Kirk assassination
cards.teaser: The Turning Point USA CEO criticized Dave Chappelle and others after the comedian made light of her husband's killing at Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
Erika Kirk, CEO of Turning Point USA and widow of Charlie Kirk, condemned comedians and commentators for joking about her husband's assassination, calling such humor "beyond disgusting." Her statement followed Dave Chappelle's Saturday night performance at Madison Square Garden, where he said he felt better since Kirk's killing and joked that Kirk is "looking up at us right now, laughing so hard he can't breathe," according to fan videos circulating online.

Charlie Kirk, 31, was killed during a speaking event at Utah Valley University in September. Elon Musk criticized Chappelle on social media, calling him "cruel" and "just not funny anymore." Hosts of the "I've Had It" podcast also apologized for laughing at a joke about the assassination.

cards.headline: Bong Joon Ho says 'The Host' feels newly relevant as 4K restoration returns to theaters for 20th anniversary
cards.teaser: The director links the film's themes to current conflicts and pandemic experience as restored version recreates original 35mm experience.
cards.body:
Director Bong Joon Ho said his 2006 monster film "The Host" has gained new relevance as history repeats itself, citing the coronavirus pandemic and ongoing conflicts including the Iran War. "Although the film has stayed the same, the history is repeating itself and making the film relevant again," Bong said ahead of the 4K restoration's theatrical return for the film's 20th anniversary.

The restoration recreates the experience of watching a fresh 35mm print as shown at the film's Cannes premiere. Bong worked to restore the subtle color qualities from the original Fuji film stock shot with cinematographer Kim Hyung-ku, though visual effects sequences required upscaling since they predated 4K technology.

cards.headline: Amazon launches $30 streaming bundle combining five services
cards.teaser: Prime Video introduces a bundled subscription offering Starz, BritBox, AMC+, MGM+ and PBS Masterpiece at 39% off individual pricing.
cards.body:
Amazon Prime Video launched a streaming bundle offering five services for $29.99 per month through its Prime Channels hub. The package includes AMC+ Premium, BritBox Standard, MGM+, PBS Masterpiece and Starz, representing a 39% discount from the combined individual subscription cost of nearly $50 monthly.

The bundle is available with a seven-day free trial and consolidates content from all five services in the Prime Video app. Programming includes series such as "Yaga," "FROM," "Outlander," "Sherlock" and "Downton Abbey," along with films from Universal Pictures and content from the "Power" and "Walking Dead" franchises.

cards.headline: Olivia Cooke left social media ahead of 'House of the Dragon' Season 3 over toxic fandom
cards.teaser: The actress cited ugliness, racism, and misogyny in the show's fanbase as reasons for deactivating Instagram.
cards.body:
Olivia Cooke, who plays Queen Alicent Hightower in HBO's "House of the Dragon," told GQ that she deactivated her Instagram ahead of the show's third season because of toxicity in the fanbase. Cooke cited "a lot of ugliness," including racism and misogyny, and said fan theories and interpretations of her and her relationship with directors had become "not nourishing."

Cooke criticized what she called the "celebri-fied nature of being an actor," saying the focus should be on artful, creative work rather than followers or brand deals. Co-creator Ryan Condal previously described comparisons fans made between younger and adult actors as "horrible."

cards.headline: Tom Brady, Jim Harbaugh executive produce two-part Michigan football documentary for Fox Sports
cards.teaser: The series examines the program's 1997 and 2023 national championship seasons.
cards.body:
Tom Brady and Jim Harbaugh are executive producers of "The Team: Michigan Football," a two-part documentary premiering on Fox Sports this month. The series examines Michigan's 1997 and 2023 national championship seasons, exploring the tradition and pressures that shaped both teams.

Part one centers on Harbaugh's relationship with the program as a player and head coach leading to the 2023 championship. Part two focuses on the 1990s era, including the 1997 championship and Brady's rise as a player. Shadow Lion produces the documentary, with Jeff Fine as director and executive producer.

hero.headline: Seven Republican senators call for delay in GOP leadership elections
hero.body:
Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections are scheduled for Tuesday, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota is still expected to be reelected to lead the Senate GOP.

Senators Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, Rick Scott of Florida, Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, and John Kennedy of Louisiana signed a letter demanding the elections be delayed to allow more discussion about the party's performance last week. Senators Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania and Jim Banks of Indiana supported the effort in statements posted on social media. Johnson threatened to skip the vote if the delay does not happen.

The decision on whether to delay falls to conference chair Tom Cotton of Arkansas, though such decisions are usually made with leadership input. The election is expected to proceed as planned Tuesday morning unless a senator motions to delay and the motion passes with a majority, which appears unlikely given the limited number of public supporters, according to a source familiar with the planning discussions. Despite arguments that Thune should not secure his leadership position so quickly, no one has announced a challenge to him.

None of the leadership elections are competitive. Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso of Wyoming, Conference Chair Tom Cotton of Arkansas, Policy Committee Chair Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia, and Conference Vice Chair James Lankford of Oklahoma are expected to retain their positions.

cards.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
cards.teaser: The Maryland senator said he is in listening mode and has not shut the door on a potential bid.
cards.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, saying he is in listening mode and that the party should not have a coronation. The Maryland Democrat's comments come as Schumer, the current minority leader, is widely expected to lead the new Senate majority in January.

Some Democrats have withheld support for Schumer, saying they want clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years before committing. Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan reiterated Monday that she will not vote for a candidate who cannot articulate a plan, especially for the first 100 days. Schumer needs a majority of the caucus to win the leadership election at a closed-door meeting in early December.

cards.headline: House Democrats eye 2028 Senate runs in Kansas, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Florida after midterm landslide
cards.teaser: Democratic House members are considering Senate bids following the party's sweeping 2026 midterm victories, targeting seats in states once thought unwinnable.
cards.body:
House Democrats are considering 2028 Senate campaigns in Kansas, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Florida following their landslide 2026 midterm victories. A source close to Representative Sharice Davids said all options are on the table for a potential run against Senator Jerry Moran in Kansas, while Representative Don Davis is considering challenging Senator Ted Budd in North Carolina.

In Pennsylvania, multiple Democrats including Representative Chris Deluzio and former Representative Susan Wild are weighing challenges to Democratic Senator John Fetterman, who has drawn criticism for siding with Republicans on key votes. In Florida, state Representative Angie Nixon is hinting at a run against Senator Ashley Moody after losing to her by three percentage points, while Representatives Jared Moskowitz and Kathy Castor are also being mentioned as potential candidates.

cards.headline: Trump says he will not approve wind permits as part of permitting bill
cards.teaser: The president said his administration would block wind turbine permits even as the Senate prepared to vote on bipartisan energy legislation.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said Monday that his administration would not approve permits for wind turbines, a key component of a bipartisan permitting bill set for a Senate vote that evening. Trump said he still supported the legislation, which is designed to streamline approvals for energy projects, transmission lines, and data centers. His opposition to wind energy threatened to undermine Democratic support for the bill.

The Senate voted 73 to 25 for cloture on the permitting reform bill Monday night, with 22 Democrats supporting it. Earlier in the day, the administration approved 10 onshore wind projects in six states. After Trump's comments, some lawmakers said they were reconsidering their votes, with Sen. Adam Schiff saying the remarks indicated Trump had not changed course on renewable energy.

cards.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid
cards.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid

The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results. DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN.

cards.headline: Elon Musk's companies face Democratic investigations after $475 million midterm spending resulted in losses
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4
cards.body:
Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4

Armed with subpoena power, Democrats are preparing to examine Musk's Department of Government Efficiency operation, its access to sensitive government data, and whether his companies benefited from his influence over the Trump administration. More than 99 percent of Musk's traceable spending went to losing candidates, according to WIRED.

cards.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C

Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation. Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
